audit_findings.title: Historical OE crosses a major divestiture despite a null perimeter
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially contaminates historical OE comparability, growth endpoints and the 79.9% RONTA used to judge sustainable growth; the latest-year anchor is not directly affected if it contains continuing operations only.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal year 2023, the Company completed the sale of certain assets and the equity interests constituting the Company’s Applied, Food and Enterprise Services businesses (the “Business”) for approximately $ 2.27 billion in cash proceeds before transaction costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The $2.27 billion 2023 divestiture is demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether every pre-sale OE year was recast to the continuing-business perimeter. If unrecast, the historical trend and RONTA compare different businesses and could materially alter the growth scenarios even though the $471.6 million anchor uses 2025 actual OE.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate 2017-2025 OE on a documented continuing-operations perimeter, excluding the sale gain, $75.0 million Brand Fee and all discontinued-operation cash flows; then recompute trend, RONTA and scenario growth.

audit_findings.title: Recurring acquired-intangible amortization may be treated as a free add-back
audit_findings.magnitude: $335.6 million FY2025 amortization, equal to 71.2% of the $471.6 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Operating cash flow reverses noncash amortization; if economically necessary acquisition, licensing or technology-replacement spending is absent from reinvestment, OE and sustainable growth are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: Total amortization expense related to amortizable intangible assets was $ 335.6 million in fiscal year 2025, $ 359.4 million in fiscal year 2024 and $ 365.1 million in fiscal year 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The amortization amount is demonstrated, but it is not demonstrated that all $335.6 million represents economic depletion or that replacement spending was omitted. Its scale relative to OE makes the unresolved treatment material: even a fraction being maintenance expenditure could materially reduce distributable earnings and valuation.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 OE reconciliation showing the amortization treatment, identify recurring acquisition, licensing and technology-replacement cash spending, and rerun OE after deducting only the evidenced maintenance portion.

audit_findings.title: A collection-timing working-capital outflow may distort the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $96.8 million FY2025 working-capital outflow, equal to 20.5% of anchor OE; six-month 2026 accounts-receivable cash inflow was $43.916 million
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary collection delay lowers the FY2025 OE anchor and therefore every forecast OE amount and terminal value when the depressed anchor is mechanically grown.
audit_findings.evidence: The cash provided by operating activities for fiscal year 2025 was principally a result of income from continuing operations of $239.9 million, adjustments for non-cash charges aggregating to $445.9 million, including depreciation and amortization of $405.3 million, and a net cash decrease from changes in working capital of $96.8 million, primarily due to timing of collections in China during fiscal year 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2025 outflow and subsequent 2026 receivables inflow are demonstrated, but the record does not prove that the entire $96.8 million was temporary or attributable to China collections. The gross outflow is large enough relative to the $471.6 million anchor to materially affect value if a substantial portion reversed.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2025 working-capital components and China receivable collections through July 2026, normalize only the documented reversal, and rerun all scenarios while preventing the same recovered cash from also being counted in bridge cash.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded pension obligations may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $148.6 million computed net claim: $132.279 million non-U.S. pension deficit plus approximately $16.3 million net supplemental-plan obligation; approximately $1.30 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any accumulated pension deficit not already discharged through forecast OE should be deducted as a senior bridge claim ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 28, 2025, all the principal non-U.S. pension plans are unfunded.
audit_findings.explanation: The unfunded claims are demonstrated. The computed $148.6 million exposure is about 1.9% of the $7.649 billion base equity value and approximately $1.30 per share versus base value of $67.11 and market price of $130.22. Even a full additional deduction would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the July 2026 pension and supplemental-plan deficits and forecast contribution treatment; deduct only obligations not already captured in forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition earnouts may be omitted from both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.442 million recorded liability and $71.2 million maximum at July 5, 2026; approximately $0.14 and $0.62 per diluted share, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected financing-classified earnout settlements omitted from OE require a bridge deduction ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 28, 2025, the Company may have to pay contingent consideration, related to acquisitions with open contingency periods, of up to $75.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves the amount: the recorded expected liability is $15.442 million, while the contractual maximum is $71.2 million. Those amounts equal about 0.2% and 0.9% of the $7.649 billion base equity value, respectively, and neither could change the valuation conclusion even if entirely omitted.
audit_findings.action: Add the July 2026 recorded $15.442 million contingent-consideration liability to the bridge unless its expected settlement is explicitly included in forecast OE; monitor quarterly fair-value revisions.

audit_findings.title: The latest bridge is post-acquisition while the OE anchor is pre-acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $67.061 million net acquisition cash paid; $72.0 million headline cash price plus up to $8.0 million contingent consideration; net cash paid equals approximately $0.59 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-acquisition bridge reflects cash spent for ACD/Labs, while the pre-acquisition OE anchor excludes its earnings, creating a perimeter mismatch that generally understates value.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequent to fiscal year 2025, the Company completed its acquisition of Advanced Chemistry Development Inc. (“ACD/Labs”) for $ 72 million in cash paid at the closing and up to $ 8 million in contingent consideration to be paid in cash based on the achievement of certain revenue metrics through 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated, but the transaction is small relative to the valuation. Net cash paid was about 0.9% of the $7.649 billion base equity value and approximately $0.59 per share; restoring that amount alone would not change the conclusion against the $130.22 market price. Acquired earnings are not separately disclosed and therefore remain unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Create a perimeter-consistent rerun using either a pre-acquisition bridge or an OE anchor including ACD/Labs earnings, working capital and amortization; include the separately recorded earnout liability and avoid restoring both purchase cash and acquired value.
